newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Barak bids for Labour party leadership.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Barak bids for Labour party leadership.

text.p: Ex-army chief Ehud Barak said on Monday he wanted to run for prime minister in Israeli elections due in four years, and launched a campaign to succeed Shimon Peres as leader of the opposition Labour Party.
"I have decided to run for the prime ministership in the year 2000...and to that end, to run for the leadership of the Labour Party," Barak, 54, told a news conference.
Long touted as a future prime minister, Barak, like his slain mentor Yitzhak Rabin, combines an impressive military record with a daring demeanor popular among Israelis.
Barak said that he would remain a candidate even if it meant facing present party chairman Peres in internal party elections for the top spot in June, 1997.
"I have made my decision, and I will run in any case -- period," said Barak, a former commando who retired from the military in January, 1995, after 35 years of service.

Benjamin Netanyahu, 47, defeated Peres in elections for prime minister in May with a campaign that stressed the Likud leader's own record as a commando officer. Peres, although a former senior official in the defence ministry, never served in the army.

"I believe that the Labour party will return to power in the next election, and I believe in my power to bring about security, peace, and prosperity for Israel, while preserving the unity of the people," Barak said.
He said he would return Labour to "its natural place in the centre of the political map, as a party of the centre," in apparent contrast to Peres, who is considered a political dove.
Peres, 73, has refrained from announcing whether he will run again, but maintains he will continue "battling for peace".
In 1995, Barak oversaw the first handover of occupied land to the Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank town of Jericho under a peace deal negotiated with the PLO.
Rabin named him interior minister in July, 1995. After Rabin's assassination, interim prime minister Peres chose Barak to take over his vacated post as foreign minister.
